records.description:
* Team:Industrial Operations & Product Supply
* Location:Saratoga Springs
* Req ID:R53229
* Contract:Full time
* Work Pattern:Onsite

**The role**
------------

**Build our future together:**

At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. We’re hiring a Sr. Director/ Executive Director of Manufacturing Operations for our new highly automated bulk/ drug substance manufacturing plant, supporting 20–30 tech transfers a year alongside commercial delivery responsibility. GMP production will run concurrently with construction and CQV for 3–5 years. This role requires both building and operating.

 
 

This site operates on a foundation of strategy, execution, and rigor. Every function at the site owns a pyramid of metrics derived from annual goal planning that connects the site’s strategic goals to the factory floor, with performance measured back up to leadership to monitor, track, and mitigate against contingencies quantified using SMART goals in days and dollars.

 
 

The Sr. Director/ Executive Director of Manufacturing Operations owns cross-suite production performance across upstream and downstream operations in both single-use and stainless-steel suites. As the site scales to six suites, this leader is accountable for delivery of the site production plan, manufacturing cost performance, and workforce strategy, drives daily operational discipline through MDI and lean standard work, and represents manufacturing on the site Leadership Team.

 
 

**When & where:**

* Location: Saratoga Springs, New York, United States

* Work model: Monday-Friday, 8am-4:30pm
 

 

**Discover your role:**

* Own cross-suite production performance and site-wide annual batch plan attainment across all operating suites

* Lead fully integrated, operations-focused suite teams, with upstream, downstream, and support activities managed within each suite, and clear day-to-day accountability for execution, staffing, and scheduling

* Oversee these functions OpEx and CapEx budget and roadmap

* Serve as the primary responsible party for this function's alignment with the Global Center of Excellence (COE), connecting site execution back to the business-level function

* Ensure this function's metrics flow up and down through the MDI structure, connecting into the site's S&OP, AOP, and long-range planning cycles

* Champion adoption of lean principles across manufacturing including standardized work, visual controls, and a culture of continuous improvement (kaizen) as the site scales to six suites

* Lead the production plan across all suites, working with supply chain to align the supply plan to the production schedule through the site S&OP process

* Drive the site's daily MFG MDI process at the suite level surfacing, escalating, and resolving issues in real time across all shifts

* Serve as the manufacturing process and cost owner, driving cost-per-batch performance and contributing to the site Annual Operating Plan (AOP) and budget

* Manage workforce strategy and ramp for the manufacturing organization, including multi-shift staffing, hiring, training, and qualification of operators as new suites come online

* Ensure cGMP compliance, right-first-time execution, and inspection readiness on the manufacturing floor, partnering closely with Quality on deviations and batch record performance

* Champion a zero-harm EHS culture and drive manufacturing safety performance across all shifts

* Lead manufacturing operational readiness for suites entering service, partnering with Technical Services on tech transfer, process readiness, and PPQ execution

* Build and maintain a lean, scalable manufacturing organization, including area management and round-the-clock shift coverage within each suite

* Partner with quality, technical services, supply chain, environmental health & safety, and operational excellence to resolve issues quickly and operate as one aligned site leadership team

* Establish high standards for performance management and accountability; develop and retain talent; perform other duties as required

* Own a gross margin improvement program and goal for this function, contributing to the site's overall margin performance
 

 

**This role requires****:**

* B.S in engineering, life sciences, or a related technical field
 + Sr. Director: 15+ years in biopharmaceutical manufacturing, including large-molecule drug substance operations including 7+ years of progressive leadership
 + Executive Director: 18+ years in biopharmaceutical manufacturing, including large-molecule drug substance operations including 7+ years of progressive leadership
 + Level will be determined based on experience
* Financially literate, with demonstrated experience of delivering production plan attainment, managing cost per batch, and operating within an annual budget

* Experience leading the start-up and ramp of manufacturing suites or facilities

* Experience leading large, multi-shift GMP organizations and building leadership depth

* Previous people leadership/supervisory experience

Does this sound like you? Apply now to take your first step towards living the Regeneron Way! We are committed to building a workplace with an inclusive culture. Regeneron is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion or belief (or lack thereof), sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, gender reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, civil status, pregnancy or parental status, age, disability, nationality, citizenship status, ethnic or national origin, membership of the Traveler community, familial status, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law. Where required, we will provide reasonable accommodation to applicants with known disabilities or chronic illnesses during the recruitment process, unless such accommodation would impose undue hardship.

Where necessary, we disclose salary ranges for roles in all countries in which we operate. The final offer will be determined within the relevant range based on the country of employment, specific role level, and your skills and experience. In some countries, collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) may apply and influence certain elements of pay or benefits. Regeneron offers a competitive and comprehensive total rewards package which may include, depending on country and role: annual bonuses or other incentive plans, equity awards, pension or retirement benefits, 401(k) company match, health and wellness programs, fitness centers, insurance benefits (e.g. medical, dental, vision, life and disability), paid time off, and family support benefits. For additional information about Regeneron benefits in the U.S., please visit https://careers.regeneron.com/en/working-at-regeneron/total-rewards/. For other locations, additional information will be provided during the recruitment process. If you have any questions, please speak with your recruiter.

 
 

Please be advised that at Regeneron, we believe we do our best work when we are together. For that reason, many roles are required to be performed on‑site. Please speak with your recruiter and hiring manager for more information about on‑site expectations for your role and location.

 
 

As part of the recruitment process, certain background checks may be conducted in accordance with the laws of the country where the position is based. The purpose of such checks is to verify certain information prior to the commencement of employment such as identity, right to work and educational qualifications.

 
 

For jobs in Canada: this posting is for an existing position.

 
 

**Salary Range (annually)**

$207,000.00 - $407,400.00

As the site scales to six suites, this leader is accountable for delivery of the site production plan, manufacturing cost performance, and workforce strategy, drives daily operational discipline through MDI and lean standard work, and represents manufacturing on the site Leadership Team.

records.description:
RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: Relocation assistance may be availableCLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: YesCLEARANCE TYPE: SecretTRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time

**Description**
---------------

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman’s Defense Systems is looking for a **Director Mission Assurance 1** to lead the Quality and Mission Assurance organization for the Strategic Deterrent Systems Division. This leadership role is located in **Roy, Utah**. This role requires strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills to lead in a dynamic engineering and production environment. There is significant responsibility and visibility with executive leadership and the broad customer organization.

**What You'll Get To Do:**

* Defines and monitors mission assurance program specifications and processes to ensure mission success of programs.
* Performs or assures quality, risk management, safety, reliability and maintainability of program achievements, subcontractors, and suppliers in accordance with contractual requirements.
* Assesses program performance and risks and determines resources to ensure mission assurance.
* Ensures the on-time delivery of high-quality products and services that meet all contractual requirements and business objectives.
* Drives the continuous improvement of people (to include training & development), products, processes, systems and services through the application of world class manufacturing to include innovative technologies, lean principles, six-sigma projects, and common best practices.
* Develops, maintains, and ensures compliance with mission assurance programs, policies, processes, procedures and that the performance and quality of products/processes conform to established standards, specifications and agency guidelines.
* Provides expertise and guidance in interpreting policies, regulatory and/or governmental regulations, and agency guidelines to assure compliance.
* Provides leadership that fosters an inclusive, motivated and engaged work culture.
* Supports the development phase of programs by assuring engineering products and processes conform to internal and customer requirements.
* Works directly with operating entities such as engineering and manufacturing to ensure that inspections, process control analyses and audits are conducted on a continuing basis to enforce requirements and compliance.
* Ensures the Quality/Mission Assurance, Manufacturing, and Engineering processes are consistent with industry capability maturity models and QMS standards (AS9100).
* Provides direct oversight in all efforts related to factory accountability and foreign object elimination practices.
* Reviews trend metrics and analyze misses in order to implement the appropriate improvements to improve performance.
* Standardizes and facilitate root cause / corrective action efforts to resolve quality issues.

As a full-time employee of Northrop Grumman Defense Systems, you are eligible for our robust benefits package including:

* Medical, Dental & Vision coverage
* 401k
* Educational Assistance
* Life Insurance
* Employee Assistance Programs & Work/Life Solutions
* Paid Time Off
* Health & Wellness Resources
* Employee Discounts

This position’s standard work schedule is a 9/80. The 9/80 schedule allows employees who work a nine-hour day Monday through Thursday to take every other Friday off. This role may offer a competitive relocation assistance package.

**You’ll Bring These Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree and 10+ years of related technical experience or a Masters with 8 years of experience
* Demonstrated experience developing, communicating and instituting new processes for an organization
* Experience managing people
* 5 years of experience in Quality Assurance or Mission Assurance specific roles
* 5 years of experience in metric development for process health and performance monitoring large programs/projects
* Leadership experience in both EMD and Production programs
* Active US Government Secret Clearance adjudicated in the last 6 years with ability to obtain SAP and Top-Secret Clearance

**These Qualifications Would be Nice to Have:**

* 10 years Executive Leadership experience, preferably within the Aerospace and Defense industry
* NG QMS familiarity
* ISO 9001 and AS9100 familiarity
* MS or MBA degree highly preferred
* Active Top Secret Clearance

Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Employees in Vice President or Director positions may be eligible for Long Term Incentives. In addition, Northrop Grumman provides a variety of benefits including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, savings plan, Company paid holidays and paid time off (PTO) for vacation and/or personal business.The application period for the job is estimated to be 20 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.Northrop Grumman is an Equal Opportunity Employer, making decisions without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, age, veteran status, disability, or any other protected class. For our complete EEO and pay transparency statement, please visit http://www.northropgrumman.com/EEO. U.S. Citizenship is required for all positions with a government clearance and certain other restricted positions.

records.title: Manufacturing Growth Program Director
records.description:
**Manufacturing Growth Program Director**

**ROLE PURPOSE** 
Provide strategic, financial, and program leadership for major manufacturing growth, capacity, investment, vertical integration, and M&A initiatives. The role connects strategy, economics, financial analysis, and operational execution to improve capital allocation, surface risks early, and enable fact-based executive decisions.

This is not a traditional PMO role. The individual will challenge assumptions, identify what does not reconcile across operational and financial information, quantify the implications, and recommend corrective action.

**Key Responsibilities**

1. Manufacturing Strategy & Investment

* Support development and execution of the multi-year manufacturing growth, capacity, footprint, and investment strategy.
* Evaluate brownfield and greenfield expansion, outsourcing, localization, make-versus-buy, vertical integration, partnerships, and acquisitions.
* Develop business cases and scenarios linking investments to capacity, revenue, margin, productivity, cash flow, ROIC, customer service, and strategic advantage.
* Assess whether proposed investments align with strategic priorities and represent the highest-value deployment of capital.

2. M&A, Vertical Integration & Strategic Transactions

* Support buy-side evaluation of manufacturing businesses, assets, technologies, suppliers, and capability acquisitions.
* Develop the strategic and economic rationale for acquisitions and vertical integration, including fit with business priorities and the expected accretive value proposition.
* Evaluate valuation assumptions, revenue and cost synergies, EBITDA and cash-flow impact, working capital, CapEx, integration costs, ROIC, NPV/IRR, and time-to-value.
* Build base, upside, and downside cases; identify key sensitivities and potential sources of value creation or destruction.
* Assess operational, financial, supply-chain, customer, technology, capacity, and integration risks during diligence.
* Support post-acquisition value-capture plans with accountable owners, milestones, and metrics for synergy and investment-thesis realization.

3. Business, Financial & Economic Analysis

* Analyze CapEx and OpEx performance against plan, approved business cases, and expected returns.
* Connect volume, mix, material, labor, productivity, utilization, yield, working capital, margin, and cash flow to operating performance.
* Apply economic thinking to capital allocation, opportunity cost, resource constraints, investment prioritization, and make-versus-buy decisions.
* Identify and quantify material variances between actual performance and the assumptions supporting approved investments.
* Develop fact-based analyses and scenarios that clarify leadership trade-offs and recommended actions.

4. Operational Insight & Pattern Recognition

* Identify patterns, anomalies, systemic gaps, emerging constraints, and leading indicators across financial and operational data.
* Challenge inconsistencies among operating results, forecasts, capacity models, project plans, and financial expectations.
* Validate key assumptions with plant, engineering, supply-chain, finance, and project teams at the source.
* Translate operating issues into their financial, customer, capacity, and strategic implications and trigger timely corrective action.

5. Program Leadership & Execution

* Monitor delivery against schedule, cost, capacity, and expected business outcomes; surface deteriorating assumptions and missed dependencies early.
* Strengthen operating reviews by focusing on variance to commitment, root cause, get-to-green actions, accountable owners, timing, and leadership support required.
* Drive transparency and accountability while maintaining execution ownership within the responsible functions.
* Apply structured problem solving to complex cross-functional issues where ownership, data, or solutions are initially unclear.

6. Executive, Board & Investment Communications

* Develop executive and Board materials covering manufacturing strategy, capacity, investments, acquisitions, operational performance, risks, and decisions.
* Prepare CIMs, investment memoranda, acquisition assessments, diligence materials, and strategic decision papers.
* Translate complex operational, financial, and technical analysis into concise business narratives that state what changed, why it matters, the quantified impact, risks, actions, and decisions required.
* Anticipate executive questions and ensure recommendations withstand rigorous analytical review.

**Candidate Profile**

Experience

* 7–10 years of progressive experience preferred; exceptional candidates with 5–7 years of highly relevant experience will be considered.
* Experience in industrial Operations, Supply Chain and Finance Operations
* Demonstrated experience evaluating acquisitions, strategic investments, or vertical-integration opportunities.
* Experience with industrial, engineered-product, manufacturing, supply-chain-intensive, or capital-intensive businesses.
* Track record leading complex cross-functional workstreams with significant financial and organizational implications.
* Experience presenting analyses and recommendations to senior executives; Board exposure is advantageous.
* Education
* Bachelor's degree in Economics, Finance, Engineering, Business, Operations, Supply Chain, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related analytical discipline.
* MBA or advanced degree in business, finance, economics, engineering, or a quantitative field is preferred but not required.

**Critical Capabilities**

**Business acumen**

Rapidly understands how a business makes money, its economic drivers, sources of competitive advantage, and where value can be created or destroyed.

**Financial and investment acumen**

Strong command of financial statements, valuation, cash flow, working capital, NPV/IRR, ROIC, sensitivity analysis, and business-case development.

**M&A judgment**

Understands buy-side diligence, investment theses, synergy assumptions, integration risks, and value-capture requirements.

**Pattern recognition**

Detects trends, inconsistencies, weak assumptions, emerging risks, and signals within complex financial and operating information.

**Operational acumen**

Understands manufacturing economics, flow, capacity, bottlenecks, productivity, investment requirements, and execution risks.

**Executive synthesis**

Distills complex analysis into clear insights, implications, recommendations, and decisions.

**Constructive challenge**

Independently validates conclusions and has the courage to challenge senior stakeholders when facts, assumptions, or performance do not align.

**Success Measures****asure**

**Investment quality**

100% of major investment and acquisition recommendations supported by a

documented strategic rationale, operational assessment, financial model, sensitivity

analysis, and risk view.

**Value realization**

Approved investments and acquisitions have baselined benefit measures, accountable owners, and a recurring cadence to track capacity, productivity, synergy, margin, cash-flow, and ROIC outcomes.

**Early risk detection**

Material schedule, cost, capacity, and value-realization risks are surfaced with

quantified impact and recovery actions before they compromise committed outcomes.

**Manufacturing readiness**

Critical-path milestones and dependencies across equipment, engineering,

supply chain, systems, staffing, training, and ramp are visible and actively managed.

**Forecast integrity**

Material deviations from approved business cases and operating assumptions are identified, quantified, and escalated through the operating cadence.

**Decision effectiveness**

Executive reviews consistently provide alternatives, economics, risks,

recommendations, and explicit decisions required, not status reporting alone.

**Communication quality**

Executive and Board materials are fact-based, concise, decision-oriented,

and supported by traceable analysis.

**Ideal Candidate**

The ideal candidate combines the mindset of a strategist, investor, economist, and operator.This individual is intellectually sharp, highly analytical, commercially minded, and comfortable operating in ambiguity. They can move from a financial model or acquisition thesis to the manufacturing floor, identify where facts do not support assumptions, and convert the insight into a compelling executive recommendation.

records.title: Sr. Director, Operations
records.description:
**About Schumacher**

Schumacher & Co. is an innovative interior design company that is disrupting the $150 billion-dollar global interior design industry. We are a technological leader on the design frontier, constantly pushing boundaries and striving for excellence. With over 500+ employees and growing, we are driven by a shared belief that design transforms life. We are dedicated to the mission of helping our customers *"celebrate the feeling of home".* F. Schumacher & Co designs and produces some of the most beautiful fabrics, wallcoverings, trims, rugs, furniture, and accessories in the world. Our portfolio of products is broad, but they are united by a passion for design, a thirst for what is next, an appreciation for what's come before, a drive to make our products with enormous care and attention for detail. F. Schumacher & Co is a globally recognized company with a myriad of showrooms both domestically and internationally.

Our competitive advantage in the industry is our people. We believe that our employees are our most important assets. F. Schumacher & Co is deeply anchored in our company's core values which are as follows:

* Preserve our Start-up spirit

* Take Ownership & Accountability

* Be Solutions-Oriented

* Demonstrate Courage

* Practice Adaptability

* Embrace Collaboration

We empower our employees to live these values daily because we understand how it will positively impact the customer's journey. F. Schumacher & Co., also known as FSCO, is the parent company to many brands within our portfolio. This role leads our **Paramount Handprints manufacturing operations** — our internal product mills based in Passaic, NJ and the Brooklyn Navy Yard — which are a critical differentiator for the business, providing craft and flexibility across our portfolio.

**Role Overview**

We are seeking an experienced, hands-on **Sr. Director of Operations** to lead manufacturing operations across our two internal product mills: **one in Passaic, NJ** which produces hand screen-printed fabric and wallcoverings in Passaic, NJ, and another in the Brooklyn Navy Yard which prints digital wallcoverings, both for FS&CO and third-party customers. This individual will oversee the full manufacturing process — from receiving and inventory through order entry, craft printing, quality assurance, shipping and client communications.

This is a builder role. The ideal candidate is scrappy and entrepreneurial, comfortable operating in a hands-on, evolving environment, while also bringing rigor, standards, and consistency to a growing operation. They will balance our commitment to craftsmanship with the need for cost efficiency and anticipate that capabilities and capacity will continue to evolve over time.

This role is based full-time, on-site in Passaic, NJ, five days a week, with occasional travel to our Brooklyn Navy Yard and SoHo locations as needed. It reports to the **Head of Portfolio Development**.

 

**What You'll Do**

* **Leadership**: Lead a team of approximately 60 across both mills.

* Directly manage the Director of Production Planning, Director of Production, Shipping & Warehouse Leads, and Senior Digital Printers at each site and indirectly oversee their teams.

* Oversee the CX leader responsible for order entry and client communication.

* Build a strong, accountable culture across both sites; recruit, develop, and retain talent at all levels.

* **Manufacturing Operations**: Oversee the end-to-end manufacturing process and P&L ownership across both sites, including:

* Warehouse receiving and inventory management

* Screen engraving, color mixing, and trialing

* Production

* Quality assurance and printing

* Cutting, packing, and shipping

* **Process improvement & margin management**: Bring consistency and standardization reliability to our operations.

* Balance craftsmanship with efficiency to protect and improve margin across the mills' output

* Identify and implement process improvements that increase throughput, quality, and reliability without compromising craft.

* Develop and manage spending against budget, in conjunction with Head of Portfolio Development

* Identify cost savings opportunities across from raw materials, vendor contracts and labor

* Develop and track KPIs across capacity, production, quality, fulfillment & financial efficiency

* **Facilities, Safety & Space Planning**

* Own facilities, maintenance, and safety programs across both mills.

* Lead space planning as capacity and capabilities evolve over time.

* Identify opportunities to augment capabilities with equipment & CAPEX investment opportunities

* **Collaboration & Communication**: Serve as an internal partner and external-facing representative of the mills, building trust with cross-functional teams as well as third-party customers and vendors.

* Build and maintain strong relationships with key customers and vendors, including third-party manufacturing and supply partners; quickly step into and manage existing external relationships as you transition into the role.

* Partner proactively with Portfolio Development, Design, Procurement, Sales and other cross-functional teams to align capacity and capabilities with business needs.

* Provide proactive, transparent communication and reporting to the Head of Portfolio Development and cross-functional stakeholders

 

**What We're Looking For**

* 8+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations leadership, ideally in a craft, custom, or make-to-order production environment.

* Ability to consistently balance productivity, quality, and craftsmanship at the highest level.

* Proven experience managing large teams (50+) across multiple functions and/or sites.

* Strong track record in process improvement and bringing standards/consistency to an evolving operation.

* Strong proactive communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.

* Excellent people management skills with a demonstrated ability to build culture and develop talent.

* Scrappy, entrepreneurial, and hands-on, balanced with the ability to bring structure and rigor; comfort operating in a business where capabilities and capacity frequently evolve

* Experience with facilities, safety, and space planning oversight.

* On-site, full-time presence in Passaic, NJ required, five days a week, with occasional travel to Brooklyn and SoHo.

* Experience with ERP or production planning software.

* Experience owning a P&L or facility-level cost-center budget.

**Nice to Have**

* Experience in screenprinting, digital printing, or textile/wallcovering manufacturing or adjacent industries.

* OSHA or manufacturing safety certification/experience.

* Bilingual (Spanish)

* Change management experience professionalizing a founder-led or informal operation.

**Benefits Package**

Your well-being is our top priority. Our benefits and total compensation are designed for the whole person, caring for both you and your family.

**Wealth Benefits:**

* Competitive Salary

* Corporate Annual Profit Sharing

* 401K Plan

**Health Benefits:**

* Dental Coverage

* Medical Coverage

* Prescription Drug Plan

* Vision Coverage

* Health Savings Account (HSA)

* TELADOC

**Other Benefits:**

* 20 Days Paid Time Off (PTO)

* 10 Company Holidays

* Bereavement Leave

* Life Insurance

* Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)

* AFLAC Plans (Accident and Critical Illness Plans)

* Pet Insurance

* Short-Term Disability (STD)

* Long Term Disability (LTD)

* Parental Medical Leave

* Child Bonding Leave

* Employee Discount

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to diversity, inclusion, and equality in the workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, race, color, age, national origin, religion, physical and mental disability, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity/assignment, citizenship, pregnancy or maternity, protected veteran status, or any other status prohibited by applicable national, federal, state or local law.

records.title: Director, Quality Assurance
records.description:
Director, Quality Assurance - Homebased - Blue Bell and Rochester 
 

ICON is a global healthcare intelligence and clinical research organisation united by a mission to bring new medicines and treatments to patients faster.

 
 

As a values-driven organisation, integrity, collaboration, agility, and inclusion are at the heart of how we work and interact with each other, customers, patients and suppliers.

 
 

As a Director, Quality Assurance at ICON, you will ensure the quality and compliance of clinical trials, interpret regulatory requirements, and contribute to the advancement of innovative treatments and therapies.

 

**What You Will Do:**

Your focus will be on driving quality assurance and compliance performance, ensuring quality, and building capability across your area (specifically Imaging and Cardiac Services).
 
 
Key responsibilities include:

 

* Serving as the QA business partner to Medical Imaging and Cardiac Services leadership and teams, providing strategic guidance on quality, regulatory compliance, and emerging risk.
* Leading the development and implementation of quality assurance strategies and processes to support clinical trial activities including establishing quality priorities with leadership and integrating quality considerations into business and operational planning.
* Conducting comprehensive quality assessments and audits to ensure compliance with regulatory standards and guidelines.
* Collaborating with cross-functional teams to identify and address quality issues and implement corrective actions as needed; analyzing quality trends to identify systemic risk and preventive improvement opportunities
* Providing expert guidance and support to staff regarding quality assurance policies, procedures, and best practices.
* Contributing to the continuous improvement of quality management systems and documentation. Promote a proactive culture of quality and continuous improvement.
* Establish quality priorities with IMC leadership and integrate quality considerations into business and operational planning.
* Provide strategic oversight of the risk-based IMC audit program, including internal and vendor audits.
* Represent Quality & Compliance in strategic sponsor relationships, governance, and significant quality escalations. Support the development, interpretation, and governance of quality agreements.
 

**Your Profile:**

You will bring significant quality assurance and compliance experience, with a track record of building high-performing teams and delivering results.
 
 
Required qualifications and experience:

* Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Pharmacy, or related field; advanced degree preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of experience in quality assurance within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, Medical Imaging or CRO industry, with significant experience in a leadership role.
* Extensive knowledge of regulatory requirements and guidelines governing clinical trials (e.g., ICH-GCP, FDA regulations). Knowledge of AI governance and regulations is advantageous.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify and resolve complex quality issues.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and stakeholders.
* Strong leadership skills including cross functional management
* Willingness to travel as required (approximately 25%)
 

 

#LI-FB2

#LI-Homebased

 
 

Employment with ICON is contingent upon having the legal right to work in the country where the role is based.

 
 

**Rewards & Benefits**

ICON offers a competitive and comprehensive total rewards package designed to support your health, wellbeing, and career development.

 
 

Benefits may include:

* Competitive base salary and performance related incentives
* Health and wellbeing programmes including medical, dental, and vision coverage where applicable
* Retirement and pension plans
* Life assurance and disability coverage
* Employee assistance programmes and wellbeing resources
* Learning and development opportunities through structured training and career pathways
 

 

Benefits may vary depending on role and location.

 
 

Visit our careers site to read more about the benefits ICON offers.

 
 

**Inclusion and Accessibility**

ICON is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building an inclusive and accessible workplace where everyone feels valued and supported.

 
 

If you require reasonable accommodations during the recruitment process, please let us know or submit a **request** .

Salary Range

$147,112.00-$183,890.00

records.title: Plant Manager II
records.description:
**Description**

**Plant Manager II**

At Pilgrim’s, *Safety Is A Condition*, which means the safety of our team members comes first - always.

Pilgrim’s is seeking a **Plant Manager II** to lead and direct overall operations of a poultry processing facility. This role is responsible for ensuring production, quality, safety, and financial objectives are achieved while maintaining operational efficiency and controlling costs. The Plant Manager II provides leadership across all plant functions, including production, maintenance, purchasing, accounting, administration, and continuous improvement initiatives, while developing high-performing teams and driving operational excellence.

The **Plant Manager II** oversees a diverse leadership team and is accountable for plant performance, regulatory compliance, team member safety, product quality, customer satisfaction, and profitability. This position partners closely with corporate and complex leadership to execute strategic initiatives, support business growth, and foster a culture of accountability, engagement, and continuous improvement. If you're a results-driven leader with a passion for people development and operational excellence, this is an opportunity to make a significant impact within one of the industry's leading food companies.

**Responsibilities & Essential Duties:**

* Directs production and ensures cost effectiveness and consistency with prescribed quality, accuracy, and performance standards.
* Maintains plant property and equipment in good condition to ensure compliance with governmental regulations and to ensure effective and economical operations.
* Prepares and submits operating reports to management to inform them of the current production status and to make recommendations to improve efficiency and effectiveness.
* Assures effective customer service and relations through timely delivery of quality product.
* Selects, trains, develops, and motivates manufacturing staff to maintain plant operation.
* Assures compliance of all plant operations with company policy and federal, state, and local regulations.
* May set production and processing goals for plant.

**What You’ll Need:**

* Typically requires a minimum of 7 years of DIRECTLY RELATED experience in a poultry processing plant.
* High School Diploma/GED; Typically requires a Bachelor’s degree in a related field. DIRECTLY RELATED work experience will be accepted on a year-for-year basis in lieu of the educational requirement.

**Why Work for Pilgrim’s?**

* **Schedule:** Monday – Friday with occasional weekends.
* **Benefits**: Vision, Medical, and Dental coverage begin after 60 days of employment;
* **Paid Time Off:** Sick leave, vacation, company observed holidays or, any other statutorily required paid leave;
* **401(k):** company match begins after the first year of service and follows the company vesting schedule;
* **Base salary** range of $148,818 - $186,761;
* **Discretionary Bonus:** This position is eligible to participate in the Company’s annual bonusplan, the amount of bonus varies and is subject to the standard terms and conditions of the incentive program;
* **Career Development:** Our company is dedicated to supporting professional growth by offering continuous learning opportunities and a focus on career growth through various learning and development programs;
* **Better Futures**

The Company is dedicated to ensuring a safe and secure environment for our team members and visitors. To assist in achieving that goal, we conduct drug, alcohol, and background checks for all new team members post-offer and prior to the start of employment. The Immigration Reform and Control Act requires that verification of employment eligibility be documented for all new employees by the end of the third day of work.

**About Us:** Pilgrim’s is a leading global food company with more than 62,000 team members worldwide. The company processes, prepares, packages, and delivers fresh, frozen, and value-added food products for customers in more than 100 countries. Pilgrim’s operates protein processing plants and prepared foods facilities in 14 states, Puerto Rico, Mexico, the U.K, the Republic of Ireland and continental Europe.

**Our Vision:** To become the best and most respected company in our industry creating the opportunity of a better future for our team members.

**Our Core Values Are:** Availability, Determination, Discipline, Humility, Ownership, Simplicity, Sincerity

**EOE, including disability/vets**

**Unsolicited Assistance:** Pilgrim's does not accept unsolicited assistance from any recruitment vendors for any of our open jobs. All resumes or candidate profiles submitted by recruitment vendors or headhunters to any employee at Pilgrim's or via the applicant tracking system, in any form without a valid written request and search agreement previously approved by HR, will be solely owned by Pilgrim's. No fees will be paid should the candidate be hired by Pilgrim's because of an unsolicited referral.

records.title: Plant Manager
records.description:
***Position Summary***

The Plant Manager is responsible for the overall day-to-day leadership and performance of the machine shop operation. This position provides hands-on leadership across machining, production, quality, maintenance, safety, scheduling, and employee development to ensure the facility consistently meets customer requirements for safety, quality, delivery, cost, and productivity.

The Plant Manager will drive operational excellence through Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, standardized work, effective production planning, and development of a high-performing manufacturing team. This individual will partner closely with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and other functional leaders to support business growth and achieve operational objectives.

***Essential Functions / Responsibilities*****:**

**Operations Leadership**

* Provide overall leadership and direction for daily machine shop operations.
* Manage production activities to achieve customer delivery, quality, productivity, and cost objectives.
* Establish and monitor daily, weekly, and monthly production goals.
* Ensure effective production scheduling, machine loading, labor utilization, and workflow.
* Identify and resolve production constraints, bottlenecks, and capacity issues.
* Ensure appropriate staffing and resource allocation to meet production requirements.
* Maintain strong floor presence and lead through visible, hands-on management.

**Machining & Manufacturing**

* Oversee CNC machining, manual machining, secondary operations, assembly, plating, Injection molding, deburring, inspection, and related manufacturing activities.
* Ensure equipment, tooling, fixtures, and processes are capable of meeting production requirements.
* Partner with Manufacturing Engineering to improve machining processes, cycle times, setups, tooling, and machine loading.
* Drive setup reduction, machine utilization, labor efficiency, and throughput improvements.
* Ensure adherence to standardized work and documented manufacturing processes.
* Lead Hazardous Waste Coordinator for facility.

**Lean Manufacturing & Continuous Improvement**

* Lead Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives throughout the machine shop.
* Implement and sustain 5S, visual management, standard work, waste reduction, and problem-solving methodologies.
* Identify opportunities to reduce scrap, rework, setup time, downtime, and overall manufacturing costs.
* Utilize data and KPIs to identify root causes and drive corrective actions.
* Establish a culture of continuous improvement and employee involvement.

**Safety & Environmental**

* Maintain a strong safety culture and ensure compliance with OSHA and company safety requirements.
* Lead safety initiatives, audits, training, and corrective actions.
* Ensure proper machine guarding, PPE, lockout/tagout, housekeeping, and safe operating practices.
* Investigate incidents and near misses and implement appropriate corrective actions.
* Hold employees and leaders accountable for safe work practices.

**Quality**

* Partner with Quality to ensure products meet customer and internal quality requirements.
* Drive reduction of scrap, rework, defects, and customer complaints.
* Ensure operators follow documented work instructions and quality procedures.
* Participate in root-cause analysis and corrective/preventive action activities.
* Promote a culture of first-time quality and process ownership.

**People Leadership**

* Lead, coach, and develop supervisors, leads, machinists, operators, and other production personnel.
* Establish clear performance expectations and accountability.
* Support recruiting, onboarding, training, cross-training, and employee development.
* Develop a flexible, multi-skilled workforce capable of supporting changing production requirements.
* Conduct performance reviews and address performance issues in a timely manner.

Required to sit, stand, bend, and lift up to 25 lbs.

* 3+ years of manufacturing leadership experience with responsibility for people and operational performance.
* Strong knowledge of CNC machining and machine shop operations.
* Experience with high-mix/low- to medium-volume manufacturing preferred.

* Demonstrated experience leading production teams and improving operational performance.

* Experience with ERP/MRP systems and production scheduling.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.

records.description:
**About the role:**
-------------------

As Plant Manager for Eaton’s Critical Power Solutions operations in Santa Ana, California, you’ll lead two facilities, 500+ employees, and approximately $280M in annual sales, delivering engineered-to-order critical power solutions for some of the world’s fastest-growing customers.

This is a **high-visibility business and operations leadership role** with the opportunity to make a significant impact. You’ll co-own the P&L, lead the full plant organization, and help scale the operation as demand continues to grow.

**We’re looking for a leader who can:**

* Build and develop high-performing, cross-functional teams.
* Deliver consistently against safety, quality, delivery, inventory, cost, and financial commitments.
* Create a culture of structured problem solving using A3, 8D, PDCA, and root cause analysis.
* Lead through growth, complexity, and change while maintaining strong operational discipline.
* Make sound financial decisions around cost, budgets, capital, capacity, and profitability.
* Move comfortably between the manufacturing floor, customer conversations, and senior leadership discussions.

**What you will do:**
---------------------

**Lead people and culture** 

* Build a safety-first culture where every employee owns EHS, and keep our safety management systems strong through active, visible leadership.
* Be a visible leader on every shift: communicate openly, spend real time on the floor, and build an inclusive team where people want to stay and grow.
* Model Eaton's values and Code of Ethics in how results get delivered, every day.

**Run a high-performing operation** 

* Co-own the site P&L and scorecard (safety, quality, delivery, inventory, cost, productivity and engagement), set stretch goals and close gaps quickly.
* Turn the division strategy and annual profit plan into clear short- and long-term site plans and run a disciplined daily management rhythm to deliver them.
* Lead demand, capacity and inventory planning (our Sales, Inventory and Operations Planning process) so we keep our commitments to customers and to the business.

**Put customers first** 

* Protect on-time delivery and shorten engineered-to-order and configure-to-order lead times so we win new business and grow with our customers.
* Partner with Sales, Marketing, Engineering, Project Management and Supply Chain to deliver end-to-end quality and customer satisfaction.

**Improve continuously** 

* Use the Eaton Business System and our continuous improvement tools to make lasting gains in safety, quality and productivity.
* Develop lean experts and problem-solvers on every shift, coach leaders to teach problem solving, and recognize teams that improve their own work.

**Grow the site** 

* Lead capacity expansion and footprint plans, including capital projects, new lines and cell layouts, automation and new product launches with Engineering.
* Represent Eaton in the Santa Ana community and build strong relationships with local stakeholders.

**Qualifications:**
-------------------

**Basic qualifications** 

* Bachelor's degree in business, engineering, industrial operations, or similar fields.
* Minimum 7 years of experience with progressive levels of accountability and responsibility in Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Finance, operational excellence (OPEX) and/or related support functions in a manufacturing environment.

 
**Preferred qualifications** 

* Master's in business administration (MBA) or other master's degree from an accredited institution.
* Lean and/or Six Sigma certification (Green Belt, Black Belt or Lean Tool Expert), with a track record of deploying a continuous improvement system.

• Strong understanding of Engineered to Order (ETO) and Configure to Order (CTO) business • Strong MRP / ERP platform knowledge, such as SAP or Oracle. 

* Bilingual (English and Spanish).

**Additional Information:**
---------------------------

* This role will be based at our manufacturing plant in Santa Ana, California.
* Relocation will be offered for this position.
* Eaton will not consider applicants for employment, immigration sponsorship or support for this position. This means that Eaton will not support any CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT plans, F-1 to H-1B, H-1B cap registration, O-1, E-3, TN status, I-485 job portability, etc.
* Travel required up to 25% (domestic).

All positions may require participation in video and in-person interviews as part of the hiring process. All candidates will be evaluated based on job-related competencies, and all candidates’ privacy rights and data security will be protected in accordance with applicable laws.

At Eaton, we strive to provide compensation and benefits that attract, engage, and retain the best talent. This includes competitive pay and a variety of benefit programs for eligible employees. The expected annual salary range for this role is $190000 - $278000 a year. This role is also eligible for a variable incentive program. *Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.*

We are committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities for all job applicants and employees. Employment decisions are based upon job-related reasons regardless of an applicant's race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, marital status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by law.

Eaton believes in second chance employment. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction history will be considered regardless of their arrest or conviction history, consistent with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, the California Fair Chance Act and other local laws.

You do not need to disclose your conviction history or participate in a background check until a conditional job offer is made to you. After making a conditional offer and running a background check, if Eaton is concerned about conviction that is directly related to the job, you will be given the chance to explain the circumstances surrounding the conviction, provide mitigating evidence, or challenge the accuracy of the background report.

To request a disability-related reasonable accommodation to assist you in your job search, application, or interview process, please call us at 1-800-836-6345 to discuss your specific need. Only accommodation requests will be accepted by this phone number.

We know that good benefit programs are important to employees and their families. Eaton provides various Health and Welfare benefits as well as Retirement benefits, and several programs that provide for paid and unpaid time away from work. Click here for more detail: Eaton Benefits Overview. Please note that specific programs and options available to an employee may depend on eligibility factors such as geographic location, date of hire, and the applicability of collective bargaining agreements.

records.title: Plant Manager (Yokosuka, Japan)
records.description:
**NORESCO, an OPTERRA Company**, helps customers modernize aging building systems and upgrade energy and water infrastructure to meet evolving demands. We implement innovative energy efficiency, distributed generation, energy storage, and renewable energy solutions that optimize the operational efficiency and improve resilience of buildings, campuses, military installations, and communities.

We are seeking an on-site Project Manager to oversee all preventive, corrective, and major maintenance activities (including repair and replacement work) at NORESCO’s 40 MW electric and thermal production facility at Yokosuka Naval Base, Japan. The cogeneration plant (CGS) is a critical asset for the base and daily operations are conducted by Navy personnel in partnership with NORESCO and our subcontractors.

NORESCO constructed the plant, which generates 50Hz and 60Hz power as well as a combination of Soft and Pure Steam, in 2008 under a Federal Energy Savings Performance Contract (ESPC). The plant pays for itself out of energy savings which NORESCO has guaranteed for the past 18 years. In order to meet our savings and availability guarantees, we employ a robust preventive maintenance program which relies heavily on Long Term Service Agreements (LTSAs) for all major pieces of equipment.

This is a Senior level position reporting to NORESCO’s Operations Manager and is administered through a 3 to 5 year International Assignment Agreement (IAA). This agreement is negotiated with each of our employees working Outside of the Continental Unites States (OCONUS). The agreement includes consideration for overseas pay, benefits, healthcare, housing, food, travel, vacation, stateside visits, relocation, etc., and is customized to the unique requirements of each new hire.

You will be the primary liaison between our NAVY customers, Japanese operators and subcontractors, as well as NORESCO team to ensure contractual obligations are met. While many of the team members in Japan speak English or are Bi-Lingual, some are not. Translators are available to facilitate conversations or process written correspondence as necessary. Japan is an amazing culture with many unique customs and protocols, a willingness to learn and adapt to their approach is an important part of your success.

It is of utmost importance for you to possess good listening, communication, and computer skills in addition to being proactive, organized, and having a bias for action. The Yokosuka Project Manager is supported by (and in-turn supports) many other NORESCO departments; Development, Engineering, Commissioning, O&M, M&V, Accounting, Legal, etc. Cross-functional technical skills, adaptability, versatility, and a quest for continuous learning and integration of advances are key in this position.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Overall contractual responsibility for plant maintenance and repair activities through careful management of Long-Term Service Agreements (LTSAs) and work orders.
* Ensuring subcontractor work is performed in a safe and professional manner with materials that meet or exceed applicable Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) and Regulatory standards.
* Participate in scheduled operations meetings and coordinate upcoming maintenance activities within the defined expectations and constraints of the customer and subcontractor availability.
* Prepare and distribute standard monthly reports (that summarize operations, maintenance, and repair activities) to NORESCO management, key customer contacts, and other stakeholders.
* Review plant operations logs, alarms, and performance data on a regular basis to evaluate equipment condition, collaborate with NORESCO team to identify potential issues.
* Perform plant inspections and safety walkthroughs during regular operations, confirm changes in equipment line-up, and subcontractor compliance with typical maintenance activities.
* Support Profit and Loss (P&L) management; assist with generating and maintaining the annual budget; capital expenditure planning; monthly forecasts, accruals, and variance analysis with development of recovery plans as needed to deliver the target revenue and profit.
* Review service agreements/proposals with manager; generate purchase orders as required; provide initial review and approval of invoices for materials and services.
* Collaborate with LTSA contractors to plan work and identify resources required for shutdown tasks such as parts, tooling, equipment, materials, and work procedures. Review and confirm subcontractors’ detailed work plans meet the customer and project needs.
* Maintain NORESCO’s Computer Maintenance Management System (CMMS) to generate reports for maintenance schedules, completion status reports, equipment histories, and forecasts.
* Coordinate with subcontractors, visitors and customers to ensure protocols are followed on matters related to site access, security clearance, safety measures, and work permits.
* Monitor warranty programs to ensure the planned and required coverage is maintained by complying with all warranty requirements. Ensure warranty work is claimed in a timely manner, and all warranty issues are resolved to minimize out of pocket expenses.
* Monitor and analyze facility performance and host data for equipment and systems condition assessments. Review finings with Operations Manger and adjust maintenance plans accordingly.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelors degree, Associates degree, or equivalent Technical Training (ex; Navy Nuclear)
* 5+ years of experience in one of the following fields; electric power generation, cogeneration, industrial utility, or district energy industry with strong working knowledge of equipment
* Ability to obtain a Federal Security Clearance for work at Government facilities.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**:

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, project management discipline or equivalent experience
* High level communication, leadership, technical, and project management skills.
* Strong sense of ownership and focus on maintaining; a Safe work environment, Uninterrupted Plant operations, Quality control, Project schedule, Resolving issues in a timely manner, and consistently meeting deadlines and commitments.
* Graduate degree in engineering or business administration
* Strong interest in engaging operators, customers, and partners to grow relationships.
* Advanced knowledge of one or more facets of Engineering or Central Plants operations; design principles, technologies, equipment maintenance and troubleshooting.
* Energy optimization, utility rates, energy costs, applicable codes, design guides, and standards.
* Robust combination of business acumen, risk management, and strategic thinking skills.
* US military or DOD project management experience, Japanese language skills, and international work experience are a plus.

**Physical requirements include:**

* Ability to climb stairs and fixed ladders.
* Ability to access rooftops and elevated work areas while following safety protocols.
* Ability to work at heights and in confined or industrial environments as required.
* Ability to maintain balance and mobility while navigating mechanical, utility, and production areas.

**Compensation:**

* $130,000 – $150,000 per year, depending on experience + bonuses

**Benefits:**

* HSA Medical insurance, with a choice of 2 buy-up options
* Dental insurance
* Vision insurance
* 100% Safe Harbor 401(k) match
* 100% company paid Life insurance
* 100% company paid Long-term Disability insurance
* Short-term Disability insurance
* Flexible Spending Account
* Commuter Benefits
* Legal and Identity Protection
* Pet Insurance Coverage
* Fertility and Reproductive Health
* Generous Paid Time Off, including Holiday, Vacation, and Sick Pay

records.title: Plant Manager
records.description:
**Position Summary**
====================

Oversee the assigned plant’s operations and maintenance delivered by the third-party operations and maintenance contractor (the Contractor) and take Company-level responsibility for safe, reliable, efficient and cost-effective power generation. Protect equipment condition and monitor delivery against agreed production, availability and contractual targets. Oversee plant resources, costs, records and stakeholder interfaces from commissioning and operational handover through ongoing operation.

The Contractor retains day-to-day operational control, provides the workforce and executes routine plant activities under the agreed contract. The Plant Manager is responsible for ensuring that the Contractor delivers plant results in line with the contract, overseeing its performance, giving technical and operational instructions to its site management as the contract allows, deciding the critical matters, and intervening when safety, performance, equipment integrity or delivery is at risk.

**Key Responsibilities**
========================

* Lead plant readiness for commissioning and operational handover with Projects, Technical, HSE and the Contractor, ensuring personnel, training, procedures, spares, maintenance systems and emergency plans are ready.
* Drive closure of handover gaps and punch-list items before and after operational handover.
* Review and approve production and operating plans prepared with the Contractor, considering demand forecasts, available capacity, equipment limits and project commitments.
* Monitor generation, availability, reliability, capacity factor, heat rate, fuel and auxiliary consumption and forced-outage performance against targets; require corrective and improvement actions from the Contractor and verify they achieve the intended results.
* Oversee heat rate improvement and auxiliary consumption reduction initiatives with the Contractor and Technical teams, and obtain approval for proposed modifications under the change management procedure.
* Review the effect of startup/shutdown cycles and load-following operation on equipment life, thermal fatigue and availability, and agree operating and maintenance strategies with the Contractor and OEMs accordingly.
* Hold daily operating coordination and plant performance reviews with the Contractor’s management, resolve operational conflicts and maintain plant risk and action registers.
* Review and approve preventive, predictive and corrective maintenance plans, overhaul scopes and outage schedules prepared with the Contractor, taking account of OEM guidance, asset condition, warranty terms, production commitments and approved budgets.
* Oversee gas and steam turbine lifecycle management with the Contractor and OEMs, including tracking of life-limited parts, rotor and stator life and fatigue effects, and integrate it into maintenance and capital planning.
* Oversee maintenance and repair execution for work quality, timely completion and minimum disruption to generation; require recovery plans or changes to resources or work methods when delivery is at risk.
* Lead the response to major equipment failures with the Contractor’s specialists, Company engineers and OEMs: approve containment and recovery actions, ensure root cause analysis is completed and authorize safe return to service.
* Oversee the Contractor’s management of spare parts, consumables, chemicals and lubricants; set critical stock priorities, resolve shortages, review technical specifications of purchase requests and ensure technical acceptance, proper storage and effective inventory control.
* Manage plant interfaces with Technical teams for utilities and shared equipment under the agreed responsibility split, and ensure assigned statutory inspections are completed with the responsible functions.
* Administer the plant O&M contract and hold the Contractor to its agreed scope, staffing coverage, service levels and technical obligations; address nonperformance with its management and require recovery plans within contractual authority.
* Prepare formal notices and claim inputs with relevant functions.
* Oversee warranty and warranty claim processes and technical disputes with OEMs and suppliers, including long-term service agreement matters, and manage technical communication with them.
* Verify the Contractor’s invoices, labor hours, overtime, reimbursable costs, materials and subcontractor charges against contract rates, authorized work and actual delivery; challenge unsupported charges and recommend verified services for approval through the Company’s payment approval workflow.
* Prepare the plant O&M budget and forecasts, control commitments and expenditure against the approved budget and act on variances.
* Evaluate additional work requests, maintain change and claim records and obtain O&M Director approval for decisions beyond approved budget or contractual authority.
* Ensure accurate production, fuel-consumption and customer and revenue meter records and timely plant reporting; provide validated data and technical explanations to Commercial and Finance for customer billing and contractual reconciliations.
* Identify gaps in O&M service capability and recommend alternative O&M contractors or specialist support to the O&M Director; contribute to technical scopes, contractor sourcing and proposal evaluation, and manage site transition and handover to preserve operating continuity when the Contractor changes.
* Oversee plant HSE requirements with HSE and the Contractor’s management, including work permits, energy isolation, waste controls and emergency preparedness; stop unsafe work and direct immediate containment and incident response under site procedures.
* Ensure plans are in place for high-risk process safety scenarios (gas or steam turbine trips, HRSG pressure events, plant blackout) and lead the response in a crisis.
* Promote a safety culture through visible leadership, participation in safety activities and training, and ensure that work is carried out with safety as an integral part of the job.
* Ensure compliance with applicable environmental permits, emission limits and monitoring and reporting requirements, in coordination with HSE and Permitting.
* Lead plant coordination with customers, grid operators and other stakeholders under agreed communication protocols, including dispatch communication and contractual availability and performance obligations.
* Ensure the plant meets grid operator and off-taker requirements for frequency, voltage, reactive power and load-change capability.
* Lead inspection and audit preparation and ensure responsible parties complete corrective actions, records and required submissions.
* Review the Contractor’s staffing and shift plans against contract requirements, require adequate competence and coverage and resolve staffing deficiencies through its management. Recruitment, payroll and employment administration remain with the Contractor.
* Ensure accurate operating, maintenance and equipment records and timely daily, weekly and monthly performance reports, including capacity utilization analysis, to the O&M Director.
* Ensure plant administrative, operating and maintenance procedures and documentation are established and aligned with applicable safety, environmental and quality management system requirements, and follow the Company’s risk management approach.
* Contribute to short, medium and long-term plant strategy, including reliability and capital investment planning, with the O&M Director.

**Required Qualifications**
===========================

* Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical, Electronics, Energy Systems, Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline preferred.
* Minimum 10 years of power generation O&M experience in natural gas-fired combined cycle plants, with responsibility for plant operations, maintenance and technical team leadership.
* Hands-on knowledge of combined cycle systems, including heavy-duty gas turbines, HRSGs, steam turbines, generators, water and steam chemistry, balance-of-plant equipment and DCS controls, with the ability to lead complex troubleshooting.
* Prior Plant Manager, Operations Manager or Maintenance Manager experience at a combined cycle plant.
* Experience with the gas turbine technology installed at the assigned plant (for example Siemens Energy or GE frame units).
* Experience planning and managing major outages and inspections (combustion, hot gas path, major overhaul) with OEMs and multiple contractors.
* Experience overseeing an outsourced O&M contractor or equivalent contract oversight, including performance management, labor-hour and invoice control, budgets and reporting.
* Experience with OEM long-term service agreements and warranty management.
* US operating experience, including independent power producers or owner-side operations.
* Working knowledge of NERC reliability requirements as applicable, environmental permit and emissions compliance, lockout/tagout and permit-to-work systems, and EHS regulations.
* Understanding of power market operations, including dispatch, availability obligations and commercial reporting to customers.
* Competence in CMMS and reporting tools; fluent English and MS Office proficiency.
* Training or certification in combined cycle O&M, leadership and team management, and problem-solving and decision-making techniques is preferred.
* Authorization to work in the United States. Ability to work at the assigned US site, travel as required.

records.description:
Plant Manager

**Company:** Smitty Bee Honey - Defiance, IA

**Reports to:** President

Job Summary

SBH is seeking an experienced, results-driven Plant Manager to coordinate and direct all major plant functions. You will oversee manufacturing, maintenance, and warehouse operations while fostering positive employee relations and managing operational budgets. The ideal candidate will ensure strict compliance with SBH policies, food safety regulations, and legal requirements, while driving continuous improvement and on-time customer delivery.

Key Responsibilities

* **Operations & Production Management:** Oversee daily manufacturing, maintenance, and warehouse operations, ensuring production schedules and product quality consistently meet specifications.
* **Customer Fulfillment:** Coordinate and communicate scheduled open orders to guarantee on-time delivery to all SBH customers, supporting strategic efforts to retain existing business and generate new sales.
* **Continuous Improvement & Efficiency:** Identify and implement initiatives to reduce labor costs, material waste, and indirect expenses. Develop and manage labor utilization strategies that adapt effectively to shifting production demands and deadlines.
* **Equipment & Facility Optimization:** Partner with Engineering and Maintenance to minimize equipment downtime. Manage process flows, optimize plant layouts, and coordinate shutdowns and startups for new production lines and equipment installations.
* **Food Safety & Quality Culture:** Champion a strong food safety culture by ensuring strict site-wide adherence to Food Safety, Quality, HACCP, and Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs).
* **Workplace Safety:** Actively monitor, support, and enforce all plant safety objectives and regulatory standards.
* **Financial & Budgetary Oversight:** Consult with the SBH President on operational budgetary planning, forecasting, and disciplined spending.
* **Team Leadership & HR Partnership:** Collaborate with Human Resources on policy development, employee relations, talent development, and workforce motivation. Clearly communicate changes in company policies, procedures, and strategies to management and plant personnel.

Qualifications

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Operations Management, Business, Engineering, or Supply Chain Management preferred (equivalent relevant work experience will be considered).
* Experience:
* 5+ years of leadership experience within a manufacturing environment required.
* Prior food processing plant management experience in an HACCP- and GMP-regulated environment.
* Certifications & Knowledge: Strong working knowledge of HACCP, GMPs, and chain-of-custody management; current forklift certification (or willingness to obtain certification upon hire).
* Skills: Proven ability to communicate clearly, lead effectively, and influence team members across all levels of the organization.

Physical Requirements

* Frequently required to stand, walk, sit, talk, hear, bend, stoop, and kneel; occasionally required to climb, balance, crouch, and crawl.
* Frequently required to push, pull, lift, and carry up to 60 pounds with assistance.
* Routinely required to reach with hands and arms, involving repetitive motion of the wrists, hands, and fingers.
* Occasionally required to maintain balance while ascending or descending ladders or open stairs.
* Specific vision abilities required include close, distance, color, and peripheral vision, as well as depth perception and the ability to adjust focus.

Work Environment

* Active, fast-paced manufacturing and production floor with heavy forklift traffic and moving machinery; constant situational awareness is essential.
* Exposure to varying climate conditions, including wet surfaces, temperature extremes (hot, unconditioned environments), and high noise levels.
* Strict adherence to food safety and PPE protocols is mandatory, including wearing hairnets/beard nets and following rigorous hand-washing procedures (safety training is provided).

Pay: $90,000.00 - $113,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Relocation assistance

Work Location: In person

records.description:
POSITION TITLE: Plant Manager 
CLASSIFICATION: Exempt 
REPORTS TO: Plant Manager I 
SUPERVISES: Yes

POSITION PURPOSE: 
Responsible for overseeing and supervising the manufacturing and distribution departments by establishing, monitoring and enforcing policies and procedures to ensure that departments run smoothly and are aligned to quality standards. Creates and executes on strategies and policies for company growth. 
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND BASIC DUTIES: 

* Oversee and supervise the Manufacturing and Distribution departments.
* Provide for the timely manufacture and distribution of product against customer orders.
* Anticipates and tracks operational and tactical risks and providing strategic solutions.
* Plays a significant role in long-term planning, project status reporting, and implementing change control processes.
* Maintain average workdays to manufacture and ship all published catalog items.
* Maintain average workdays to manufacture and ship all custom manufactured items (RCC label)
* Provide monthly responses to budget variance.
* Provide for utilization planning by weekly reporting of the average Work-in-Process.
* Perform physical inventories of raw materials, packaging components, and finished goods.
* Provide for an appropriate balance of inventory to meet performance and financial objectives.
* Implement plant safety programs and ensure compliance with GMP.
* Confirm that appropriate work instructions are developed and maintained and followed throughout the business.
* Ensure that all ISO quality systems are followed.
* Provide compliance to ISO quality systems (i.e. Corrective Action)
* Oversee facilities and grounds maintenance.
* Oversees and reports weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual metrics.
* Identifies trends and assess opportunities to improve processes and execution.
* Completes reasonability testing and information validation prior to circulating findings and recommendations to key stakeholders.
